messages.content: How big is the games market in 2026, and which part is biggest?

Newzoo forecasts about **$213.9B for 2026 (+6.1%)** [S], as of its Aug 2026 summary:

- Mobile: $121.1B (+6.8%)
- Console: $46.9B (+5.1%)
- PC: $45.9B (+5.3%)

Mobile is more than half the market. Two cautions: Newzoo revised 2025 from $188.8B to a final $201.6B within a year, so always quote the edition and date; and app-store trackers like Sensor Tower show mobile in-app spend roughly flat (H1 2026 ≈ −2%) because they don't count web shops or China Android.

For you: the money is on phones, and growth now comes from existing players spending more, not new players arriving.
Newzoo says mobile is growing ~7% but I read mobile game revenue fell in H1 2026. Which is right?

Both can be right because they measure different things.

- **Sensor Tower (H1 2026):** mobile game in-app purchases ≈ $39.8B vs $40.6B a year earlier (about −2%), downloads ~−12% [S]. It only counts the App Store and Google Play.
- **Newzoo (2026 forecast):** mobile $121.1B, +6.8% [S]. It also counts direct-to-consumer web shops, third-party Android stores and China Android.

So app-store spend is flat; growth is happening off-store. Don't pick one silently. Say which you're quoting and why. For a Roblox dev, the most relevant number is neither: read Roblox's own bookings in its quarterly letter [P].
Roblox DAUs went from 151.5M in Q3 2025 to 123M in Q2 2026. Is Roblox dying? Should I leave?

No, but it's a real slowdown, and you should understand why.

- Q2 2026: 123M DAU (+10% YoY), bookings $1.56B (+8%) [P]. Q3 2026 bookings guidance: −14% to −18% YoY [P].
- The comparison base is inflated: Q3 2025 had viral hits (Grow a Garden, Steal a Brainrot).
- Roblox's stated reasons [P]: mandatory age checks for chat, lower spend per hour from younger US/Canada players, players moving to evergreen games, and a recommendation change that now rewards 28-day retention.

It's still the largest under-13 platform and paid creators $1.5B in 2025 [P]. Don't leave. Adjust: build for retention, expect lower spend per kid, and read the Q3 letter (due Oct 29, 2026 [S]) before planning your next update.
Should I time my tower-defense update launch around GTA VI?

GTA VI is listed for **Nov 19, 2026** on PS5/Xbox Series X|S in Take-Two's latest 10-Q [P]. It's an adult-rated game, so it doesn't compete directly for your under-13 players.

What it does affect:
- YouTube and TikTok gaming feeds will be crowded in late Nov–Dec, so organic reach for anything aimed at teens drops.
- Older siblings and parents will be busy with it.

Practical call: launch your update **before Nov 19** or after the first two weeks of hype, and aim your marketing at younger kids. Then compare your Roblox dashboard week over week to see if it changed anything. There's no published data on GTA VI's effect on Roblox, so measure it.
Why does everyone say the live-service market is saturated?

Because players' time is already taken by old games.

- On PC/console, new releases get only ~13% of playtime, flat for three years; the top 20 franchises still take more than half (Newzoo PC & Console Report 2026) [S].
- In 2025 Roblox became the most-played title by hours (+52%), while Fortnite (−29%) and Call of Duty (−33%) fell [S].
- Many 2025–26 live-service launches lost most players or shut down (e.g. Anthem servers closed Jan 2026) [U].

Lesson for a solo dev: don't try to be someone's "forever game" from scratch. Build inside a platform where kids already spend time, and design for short sessions that fit around their existing habits.
Which regions are growing fastest and should I care as a Roblox dev?

Newzoo 2026 [S]: Middle East & Africa +10.3% ($8.5B) and Latin America +7.9% ($9.3B) grow fastest, but Asia-Pacific is biggest ($100.7B, 47%). Spend per player is very uneven: roughly $227/year in North America vs ~$13 in MEA (our maths from Newzoo's totals).

On Roblox specifically, Q2 2026 DAUs grew 67% in Japan and 64% in India vs 6% in US/Canada [P].

Yes, care, because players there can boost your CCU and ranking. But expect lower revenue per player. Cheap wins: icon-first UI, simple translations, and making sure your game runs on low-end phones.
My friend says 'the games market is $300 billion and growing 15% a year, so any game will make money.' Is that right?

No, on both counts.

- Size: Newzoo puts 2026 at about **$213.9B**, growing **~6%** [S]. I don't know a credible source for $300B/15%; ask where it came from.
- "Any game will make money": the market is concentrated. On PC/console the top 20 franchises take more than half of playtime and new releases ~13% [S]. On Steam, ~20,000 games launched in 2025 and the median earned very little [U].

A big market doesn't mean a big share for you. What matters is your niche's size and competition. Measure that with a top-20 CCU snapshot of your genre on Roblox.
Why did consoles get more expensive in 2026 and does it matter for my Roblox game?

Memory chip prices jumped (AI data centres are buying it up), plus tariffs. Nintendo raised the US Switch 2 price from $449.99 to $499.99 on Sept 1, 2026 and cut its Switch 2 sales forecast [S]. PS5 and Xbox prices also rose; reported figures vary, so check official stores [U].

It matters indirectly: pricier consoles push more kids to the device they already have, usually a phone or tablet. Mobile is ~84% of players worldwide [S]. Keep your game mobile-first and light enough for cheap phones.
What's the US games market like right now?

Circana/ESA (Feb 2026, restated Mar 2026) [S]:
- 2025 US spending: **$60.7B** (+1.4%), restated to $60.8B. Second-highest ever after 2021.
- Subscriptions +20%; mobile ~+1%; physical sales at a 30-year low.
- **Roblox was the #1 game by US retail dollar sales in 2025** (gift cards), with Roblox gift-card spend +16%.
- Circana forecasts $62.8B in 2026, helped by GTA VI.

The Roblox gift-card point matters for you: many kids' purchases start with a parent buying a card, so parents are part of your audience. Be clear and fair about prices.
Is it a bad time to try to get a games industry job instead of going solo?

It's a hard job market. Data as of 2026:
- GDC 2026 survey: 28% of developers were laid off in the past two years (33% in the US) [S].
- Layoff trackers count ~9,200 job cuts in 2025 and project ~13,800 for 2026 as of Oct 2026 [U]; projections have swung a lot.

That doesn't mean "never apply". It means a shipped game with real players and retention numbers is your best CV either way. Building on Roblox gives you both income potential and portfolio proof. I can't predict hiring for your area; check local postings for a month to measure demand.
What percentage of the global games market is kids under 13?

I don't have a reliable global figure for that, and I won't guess.

What we do know:
- US average player age is 37 (ESA 2026) [P].
- Of age-checked Roblox users, 35% are under 13 (end of Q2 2026) [P]. That's Roblox only, and based on users who completed age checks.
- In the UK, 88% of 3–17s play games on some device (Ofcom, Oct 2026) [P].

If you need a number for a pitch, cite one of these with its scope, or use Newzoo's paid demographic data and quote it with the date.
Give me a 5-point plan for my studio based on the 2026 market.

1. **Stay on Roblox, build for retention.** Recommendations now judge games over 28 days, using play-through and first-play bounce rate [P]. Fix your first minute and give 4-week goals.
2. **Fair, small purchases.** Roblox reported lower per-hour spend from young US/CA players [P]; design so non-payers have full fun and payers get cosmetics/convenience.
3. **Mobile and low-end first.** Mobile is ~84% of players [S]; Roblox growth is in Japan and India [P].
4. **Localize with icons.** Cheap way to reach growth markets.
5. **Watch the platform.** Read each Roblox quarterly letter and DevForum announcements; Rec Room's 2026 shutdown shows platforms can change or vanish [S].

Metric to watch monthly: D7 and D30 retention in your Creator Dashboard.
